title: Introduce token-route waterfall panel and dynamic log sampler
author: Maya Desai
description: Adds a new observability dashboard panel (Token Route Waterfall) and a dynamic in-service log sampler to reduce log volume while preserving SLO-relevant traces. Motivation: long tail token-cost and latency spikes require a concise view that ties model route, kernel queueing, and token phase timings into a single waterfall so SREs and runtime engineers can root-cause bursty cost spikes. The log sampler uses a risk score derived from: token cost delta, model variant fallback, kernel queue latency, and recent SLO proximity to tune sampling rate per-invocation. Also adds a small background job that computes warmup effectiveness for prefetch caches and surfaces heatmap metrics for prompt-shape warmups. The change includes dashboard JSON, a UI renderer component, backend metric adapters, tests, and docs. Key behavioral notes: sampler defaults to conservative sampling in beta; sampling decisions are annotated into traces for post-hoc correlation; waterfall supports per-tenant and per-model rollups.
commits: 4 commits: 1) Add waterfall panel JSON and UI renderer (initial scaffold). 2) Implement dynamic log sampler and risk scorer (w/ feature flag). 3) Add warmup effectiveness heatmap job and metric adapters. 4) Tests, docs, and changelog updates.

notes: Runtime impact: dynamic sampler runs in the telemetry path with bounded CPU; default off in low-tier accounts. Ops: add 'sampler.clamp_pct' to tenant config for control if needed.
